verdicts.rationale: A is a single chapter ("Sources of immunity to error through misidentification", pp. 158-179, own DOI) inside the book B ("Immunity to Error Through Misidentification"). A's booktitle equals B's title. Chapter vs whole edited volume — different bibliographic objects.

Identical title "Rules and Representation(s): Chomsky and Representational Realism", same author Pylyshyn. 1988 unpublished manuscript vs 1991 incollection (Basil Blackwell) — manuscript then published chapter, same work.
Same title "Rules and Representation(s): Chomsky and Representational Realism", same author. 1988 unpublished vs 1991 incollection (Basil Blackwell) — preprint/published version of the same chapter.
Both "Philosophical Papers", F. P. Ramsey, 1990, Cambridge University Press. B's title trails "ed" (editor note) but is the same edited collection. Same book.
"Interactive Gesture(s) in Dialogue: a PTT Model", Rieser & Poesio, 2009, same venue (SIGDIAL 2009 / 10th Annual Meeting of SIGDIAL), identical pages 87-96. Same paper.

A is "Increasing risk: I. A definition" (1970, JET vol 2). B is the separately published "Addendum" (1972, JET vol 5, p. 306, distinct DOI). The addendum is its own short publication, not the same work.
Both "Parallel Distributed Processing" Vol. 1, Rumelhart, MIT Press; years 1986/1987 (reprint dating). Same volume of the same work.

A explicitly spans volume "1 and 2" (the complete two-volume PDP set, full-set DOI 10.7551/mitpress/5236), whereas B is "Vol. 1" only (different ISBN, paperback). A full set vs a single constituent volume is a genuinely different bibliographic object; not confident enough to merge.

A is "Parallel Distributed Processing", Rumelhart & McClelland, 1986, with the canonical PDP DOI (10.7551/mitpress/5236) and no volume specified; B is the "Vol. 1" MIT Press edition. Both denote the PDP work — merge.
"Seven Puzzles of Thought", Sainsbury & Tye, Oxford University Press, 2012/2013. Same book (A adds the subtitle "And How to Solve Them").
A is the Third Course of Lectures (Troisième cours, 1910-1911); B is the First Course (Premier cours, 1907). Different lecture courses in the Saussure series — distinct volumes.
A is the First Course (Premier cours, 1907); B is the Second Course (Deuxième cours, 1908-1909). Different lecture courses — distinct volumes in the series.

A is "Local Contexts: a Precis" (2008 unpublished), B is the full article "Local Contexts" (2009, Semantics & Pragmatics). A precis is often a distinct short published summary rather than the full paper's preprint; cannot confidently call these the same work.
"Local Contexts" (2009, Semantics & Pragmatics) vs "Local contexts and local meanings" (2010, Philosophical Studies) — different titles, journals, years, DOIs. Separate papers.
"Presuppositions and Local Contexts" (2010, Mind) vs "Local contexts and local meanings" (2010, Philosophical Studies) — different titles, journals, DOIs. Distinct papers.
A is "Super monsters II" (S&P 10.12, number 12); B's fields are "Super monsters I" (S&P 10.9, number 9). Part I vs Part II with distinct DOIs — different papers.
A is "Super monsters II" (S&P 10.12, number 12); despite the citekey, B's fields describe "Super monsters I" (S&P 10.9, number 9). By fields these are the two distinct parts — different works.

"Sign Language and the Foundations of Anaphora" (2017, Annual Review of Linguistics) vs "Visible Meaning: Sign language and the foundations of semantics" (2018, Theoretical Linguistics) — different titles, journals, years, DOIs. Distinct papers.

A "Objects and attention: the state of the art" (2001, Cognition special issue) and B "Objects and attention" (2002, MIT Press) are the journal special issue and its book reprint of the same collection by Scholl. Same work.

A "Objects and attention: the state of the art" (2001, Cognition special issue) and B "Objects and attention" (2002, MIT Press book) are the same content — the Cognition special issue reprinted as an MIT Press volume. Same work.
